newsitem.title: UK: Dollar remains easier in late Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dollar remains easier in late Europe.

text.p: The dollar remained easier in late European trading with investors nervously eyeing the U.S. asset markets for further signs of weakness. Strong data points to higher rates but will hurt the dollar as it is reacting to capital flows out of asset markets. Sterling followed the dollar down and was sharply lower on a trade weighted basis.
EUROPEAN CLOSING FOREX REPORT -
The dollar sank in late European trading after another strong piece of U.S. economic data knocked the asset markets.

Although the stronger than expected NAPM survey points to a monetary tightening sooner rather than later the dollar is reacting more to what happens with capital flows than what happens with interest rates.

"Text books that say strong figures mean higher rates and a stronger currency are useless these days," said Nick Parsons, forex analyst at Banque Paribas. "It's linked to capital flows into the bond market, particularly those from the Far East."
At 1633 GMT the dollar was at 1.5401/07 marks and 115.55/65 compared with opening levels of 1.5468/75 and 115.88/98. Ahead of the New Year holiday it closed in Europe at 1.5425/35 and 115.88/93.
The December NAPM showed that manufacturing accelerated strongly and pointed to good economic growth in 1997.
The index of manufacturing activity rose to 54.0 from 52.7 in November, well up on the 51.5 figure expected by the market.
This on top of Tuesday's strong home sales and consumer confidence figures has convinced many that the FOMC meeting in February will decide to raise rates to fend off inflation.
Other data today had U.S. jobless claims up at 366,000 in week to December 28 from revised 344,000 in the previous week and compared with a market forecast for 334,000.
There is little in the way of U.S. data on Friday and volume should remain fairly low, dealers said.
Many investors have extended the New Year break into the weekend and it will not be until Monday that volume returns to anything like normal, they said.
Underlying dollar bullishness will remain, however, with the yen and mark both looking vulnerable to further declines, analysts said. But weak U.S. asset markets will hurt the dollar.
Sterling declined alongside the dollar with cable coming down to a late $1.6866/76 from an opening $1.7036/46 and Tuesday's close of $1.7080/85.
"When the big figure went cable really started to slide and sterling mark came down with it," said one trader.
Sterling is vulnerable because everyone is long but cable did managed to bounce off trendline support at 1.6840 in late business.
Sterling/mark also took a hit to 2.5965/70 from and earlier 2.6360/70. Sterling trade weighted index crahsed 1.1 point to close at 95.0.
The mark was basically steady but below earlier highs after a firm start.
It was at 3.3702/07 French francs after closing at 3.3718/22 on Tuesday.
The lira stayed firm, rising to 984.00/50 to the mark from 986.30/95 earlier.
Phil Smith, London Forex desk +44-171-542-6284.
